question: With UBER closing November 20 at $63.47 in Stage 4 (bouncing modestly to $64.60 intraday Nov 23), what do the tape and options chain demand for equity and our 5 Dec 2027 LEAPS?

epigraph.quote: A one-day bounce inside a Stage 4 breakdown is an exit window for underwater out-of-the-money calls, not a signal to catch a falling knife.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein's Stage Analysis Discipline

web_blocks.html: Fundamental quality never overrides a broken tape. On November 20, 2026, UBER closed at $63.47 (-3.25% 1D, -8.93% 1W, -19.95% 3M) [21, 24]. That confirmed a full Stan Weinstein Stage 4 (Markdown) on 30.06M shares (1.55x 20-day volume), just $0.18 above its $63.29 52-week low. Monday November 23 saw a mild +1.77% bounce to $64.60 on light volume (0.62x 30-day average). Live TradingView still enforces STAGE_4, gate CAP_REJECTED, and AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN. Every key average slopes downward above price: 50D SMA $68.80, 30W SMA $71.41, and 200D SMA $72.35–$72.40.

Weekly (1W), Daily (1D), and 4-Hour (4H) charts all show sellers in control. Through November 20, UBER logged 7 distribution days in 25 sessions, with ATR-14 at $2.42 and daily RSI at 34.08. On the live November 23 snapshot ($64.62), 4H RSI sits at 36.21 below falling 4H 20-EMA ($67.28) and 50-SMA ($67.83) lines. Daily RSI is 38.63, weekly RSI is 40.45, Bollinger width is 13.85%, and intraday_4h_turn stays false. Meanwhile, the US market sits in a confirmed Downtrend: only 35.8% of S&P 1500 stocks hold above their 50-day SMA, with 10 distribution days and a 5.04% 10Y yield [23].

web_blocks.takeaway: UBER sits in confirmed Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED) inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend (35.8% breadth >50DMA). Monday's low-volume bounce to $64.60 does not repair the broken weekly trend; new equity bids remain 0.0%.

web_blocks.html: New Options Desk Verdict (WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT_OR_BASE): Live options show elevated volatility (ATM IV 42.8% vs. HV20 34.3%, IV_ELEVATED). Buying naked calls in Stage 4 risks drawdown, vol crush, and theta decay. We commit 0% new options cash until UBER builds a Stage 1 base and reclaims >$73.50; the Feb 19, 2027 $65/$75 spread ($349 max loss = 43.7 bps of $79,861.16 NAV) in Section 13 is illustrative reference only.

web_blocks.title: Critical Independent Override: EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on All 5 Open Dec 17, 2027 LEAPS Contracts
paragraphs: Schwab and Robinhood hold 0 common UBER shares (NOT_HELD). Robinhood holds 5 Dec 17, 2027 Call LEAPS: 4x $110C ($2,644.91 cost; $1,307.91 book mark) and 1x $100C ($818.95 cost; $467.95 mark). Total cost is $3,463.86 and book mark is $1,775.86 (2.22% of $79,861.16 NAV), with 392 DTE as of Nov 20 (389 DTE Nov 23).

Why We Override to EXIT_IMMEDIATELY: The scanner prints HOLD only because price sits above $63.00. Independent math proves holding is a trap. At our $70.00 Base Case ($67.20 EV), both strikes expire at $0.00 (-100%). Even at our $105.00 Bull Case, all 4x $110C still expire at $0.00. Waymo breaks Austin/Atlanta exclusivity in Jan 2028, Delivery Hero closes in H2 2027, Q4 faces a ~$1.5B UK VAT drain, and AV outlays top $10B. Meanwhile, US cash sits at $7,290.91 (9.13% of NAV) versus our 22.0% floor.

Binding LEAPS Rule — EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH): Use Monday's relief bounce (~$64.60) and limit orders near mid to close all 5 LEAPS cleanly into USD cash. Salvage time value now instead of riding deep-OTM calls to zero. Execute ZERO averaging down; any print or close <= $63.00 triggers instant exit.

Rebuttal to the Oversold-Bounce Counter-Argument: Could 389 DTE calls recover intermediate delta/vega value if Q4 earnings ($63.25B–$65.25B GB guide) spark a bounce off $63.29 (RSI 34.08, ATM IV 42.8%)? Possibly—yet betting on a counter-trend bounce with recorded book marks ($1,775.86, stale vs. live chain mid) while US cash sits at 9.13% vs. the 22.0% floor risks nonlinear delta collapse if $63.00 breaks in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend. Using Monday's ~$64.60 bounce and limit orders near mid locks in salvageable USD cash cleanly.

web_blocks.html: Two concrete chart milestones must happen before we ever reconsider UBER for new common capital. First, institutional selling must exhaust itself as shares carve a multi-week Stage 1 base above $59.08–$62.17 (Pivot S2/S1). Second, UBER must reclaim both its 30-week SMA ($71.41) and 200-day SMA ($72.35–$72.40) above $73.50 on >=1.25x average volume while S&P 1500 breadth exits its Downtrend. Until both occur, new capital stays strictly on the sidelines.

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 showed you that Uber's true normalized multiple is 18.2 times AV- and SBC-adjusted free cash flow with only +5.9% expected value, Chapter 8 delivers the clearest possible verdict from the price tape. At the verified November 20, 2026 close of $63.47, Uber confirmed a full Stan Weinstein Stage 4 markdown—falling 3.25% on the day and 8.93% on the week on 30.06 million shares, or 1.55 times 20-day average volume, just 18 cents above its $63.29 52-week low. Even Monday November 23's modest +1.77% relief bounce to $64.60 arrived on weak mid-session volume (0.62x 30-day average) and failed to repair a single moving average.

Every timeframe confirms that sellers remain in control. On the weekly chart, Uber trades roughly 9.5% to 11.5% below its 30-week moving average ($71.41) with a weekly RSI of 40.45. On the daily chart, price sits well below a falling 50-day moving average ($68.80) and more than 10% below its 200-day moving average ($72.35–$72.40), with 7 institutional distribution days over the last 25 sessions and a 14-day ATR of $2.42. Even on the 4-hour chart, RSI sits at 36.21 below falling 20-EMA ($67.28) and 50-SMA ($67.83) resistance with no confirmed bullish turn. Layer that on top of a broader US market Downtrend—just 35.8% of S&P 1500 stocks above their 50-day average and 10 distribution days—and stepping in front of this tape is pure ego.

For new options trades, our stance is equally disciplined: WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT_OR_BASE—stand aside at CMP. Implied volatility is elevated at 42.8% versus 34.3% 20-day realized volatility. Buying naked calls into elevated IV during a Stage 4 downtrend exposes you to simultaneous directional loss, volatility crush, and time decay. Only if UBER tests and stabilizes above its $60.96 support shelf would a defined-risk spread (such as the February 19, 2027 $65/$75 Bull Call Spread at ~$3.49 debit, capping loss at $349) even warrant review—not today.

That brings us to the single most actionable portfolio decision in this entire dossier: our 5 open December 17, 2027 Call LEAPS contracts in Robinhood—4 contracts of the $110 strike ($2,644.91 cost; $1,307.91 recorded mark) and 1 contract of the $100 strike ($818.95 cost; $467.95 recorded mark), totaling $3,463.86 cost and $1,775.86 recorded market value (2.22% of our $79,861.16 consolidated US net worth) with 392 calendar days left as of November 20 (389 from November 23). Although the mechanical scanner prints HOLD purely because price remains above the $63.00 floor, our independent analysis overrides it to EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH).

Look at the cold math. At our independent $70.00 Base Case ($67.20 expected value), both the $100 and $110 calls expire at $0.00 intrinsic value—a 100% loss. Even in our $105.00 Bull Case, all four $110 calls STILL expire worthless. Meanwhile, Waymo breaks Uber exclusivity in Austin and Atlanta in January 2028 (weeks after expiry), Delivery Hero does not close until H2 2027, Q4 2026 absorbs a ~$1.5 billion UK HMRC VAT cash hit, and over $10 billion in AV commitments weigh on capital allocation through 2027. There is no credible catalyst to drive a +58% to +73% rally above $100–$110 before December 2027. With consolidated US cash at $7,290.91 (9.13% of net worth) versus our 22.0% Downtrend floor, using Monday's $64.60 relief bounce to close all 5 LEAPS via limit orders into USD cash is disciplined risk management—not capitulation. A fair counter-argument asks whether 389-day LEAPS could bounce in intermediate delta and vega value on an oversold Q4 earnings rally off $63.29 lows. Yet waiting for a counter-trend bounce while consolidated cash sits at 9.13% versus our 22.0% Downtrend floor exposes those deep-OTM calls to rapid delta collapse if $63.00 breaks; executing limit orders near mid on Monday's ~$64.60 relief bounce locks in cash cleanly.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: USE THE RELIEF BOUNCE TO EXIT DEEP-OTM LEAPS
book_callouts.text: When your own Base Case ($70.00) leaves both $100 and $110 calls worthless, and even your Bull Case ($105.00) leaves four of the five contracts at $0.00, holding on because of 389 days of time value is hope, not math. Sell into relief-bounce liquidity via limit orders and rebuild your cash buffer.
